Critical Vehicle Protocol

The Scooter Problem: Two Riders + 10–12" Wheels on Chame Boulders

The road from Besisahar to Chame (especially around Jagat, Chamje, and Timang) has deep glacial water crossings, loose boulders, and steep hairpins. A scooter with two riders and luggage will scrape its underbelly and overheat its CVT automatic clutch.

1. Zero Heavy Luggage on Scooter

Strap the 24-can Red Bull carton, tools, and heavy backpacks onto the two motorcycles. Unik & Ritik carry 0 kg of heavy cargo.

2. Mandatory Pillion Walk Zones

On steep switchbacks (Timang climb, Chamje waterfalls, Khangsar climb), Ritik (Scooter Pillion) MUST hop off and walk 100–300m so the CVT clutch stays cool.

3. Post-Bhai Tika Fuel Reserve

Pumps in Besisahar/Chame often close after Tihar. Fill full tanks in Dumre & Besisahar and carry plastic petrol bottles for the scooter's 5L tank.

4. Day-Before-Bhai Tika Service

Inspect and service the scooter's CVT belt, gear oil, air filter, and front/rear brake pads the day before Bhai Tika.

-12°C Morning Bike Cold-Start Trick

Pisang & Khangsar

In mid-November, night frost at Pisang (3,200m) and Khangsar (3,734m) freezes batteries and thickens engine oil. Follow this sequence so you don't drain your battery:

AMS, Manang Wine & Red Bull Rules

4,150m – 4,919m
🍷 Rule 1: ZERO Alcohol on Day 2 (Shree Kharka / Base Camp)

Alcohol depresses breathing at night and accelerates Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) at 4,150m. Save the Manang Wine party for Day 3 night back down at Pisang/Chame or at home!

⚡ Rule 2: Max 1 Can of Red Bull During the High Trek

Above 4,200m, heavy caffeine + taurine causes rapid heart rate, diuretic dehydration, and mimics altitude panic attacks. Drink Jeevan Jal (ORS) and hot garlic soup instead.

💊 Rule 3: Diamox & Cash-Only Readiness

Pack Diamox (Acetazolamide 250mg), Paracetamol, Ibuprofen & Sinex. Carry 100% hard cash from town—Chame/Manang ATMs fail and Tilicho Base Camp has no mobile data for QR codes.
